title: Heights: 'Top/Bottom of Model' include the fixtures, so cuts follow the vise

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP.

## What happens

`Top of Model` and `Bottom of Model` resolve to the bounds of **every model in the document, fixtures included**. With a vise placed, a cut referenced to `Bottom of Model` runs down to the **bottom of the vise body**, and `Top of Model` can resolve to the **jaw tops**.

Every 2D/3D milling kind defaults to these references: 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, Slot, Trace, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Engrave, Circular, 3D Pocket, 3D Finish, Deburr and Trochoidal slot (`bottom_z = bottom_of_model`, `top_z = top_of_model`), plus 2D Chamfer and Thread (`top_z`). So a default operation in a document with a vise is wrong at generate.

Cause (v0.19.0): `operation/heights.rs` resolves both references through `setup_align::solid_aabb_in` -> `model::solid_world_aabb`, which walks `model::model_entities`. `model::is_model` leaves out stock, WCS, tools, operations, setups and program entries, but **not fixtures**. The fixture's setup is not considered either.

## Reproduction (headless, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

A plain 50 x 50 x 6 mm block (STL), moved to Z 4..10. Box stock 55 x 55 x 11 (Z 0..11). WCS at the stock top centre. Tool `EM-0600-4FL`. One `2D Contour` with its defaults (top = Top of Model, bottom = Bottom of Model).

```
import_model {path: block.stl, name: block}
move_model   {name: block, position: [-25, -25, 4]}
set_stock    {box: {dx: 55, dy: 55, dz: 11}}
set_wcs      {stock_point: {x: center, y: center, z: max}}
add_builtin_vise {size: "5 in", position: [0, 27.5, -36.1], opening: 55}   # jaw tops at Z 2, below the part
add_tool     {catalog: EM-0600-4FL}
add_operation {kind: "2D Contour", tool: EM-0600-4FL, name: Op, source: block}
generate; verify; post {output: out.nc, post: Fanuc}
```

| | Bottom of Model resolves to | Top of Model resolves to | Generate | Verify / post |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No vise | Z 4 (part bottom), posted Z-7.0 | Z 10 | ok | ok, posts levels Z-1 / -6 / -7 |
| Vise below the part (jaw tops Z 2) | **Z -99.6, the vise base** (WCS Z -110.6) | Z 10 | **ok, no warning** | **blocked**: `flute at move 32 strikes a fixture`, `shank at move N strikes a fixture`, `rapid at move N strikes a fixture`, plus `shank/holder ... collides with the part or an island` (722 findings) |
| Vise fitted to the stock (`fit_to_stock: true`, jaw tops Z 38.1) | Z -63.5 | **Z 38.1, the jaw tops** | refused: `Contour: nothing to machine: no material at z = 38.100 - the source spans Z4.000 to Z10.000` | - |
| Vise declared in another setup (`add_setup Setup 2`, vise `setup: Setup 2`), op in the first setup | still the vise base | - | ok | blocked as above |

To confirm the depth, the op was generated with the vise, then the vise was untagged (`remove_fixture`; the op stays `ok`, the model stays) and posted. The post was then refused with `gouge: program cuts below the model in 3920 cell(s), worst 63.50 mm at (-27.31, -27.31, z -99.60)`. The generated path goes to the vise base, Z -99.6.

## Severity

- **The post blocks it** in every case I tried: the fixture collision check catches the flute in the vise. So no gouging G-code was written.
- **It is still wrong output at generate.** Generate reports `ok` with no warning for a path that goes 100 mm into the vise. The only signal is hundreds of verify findings that read as a collision, not "your heights point at the vise".
- In the user's project the workaround was to measure **every** height from Top of Stock.
- The safety still depends on the fixture check catching every case. A fixture tagged in another setup still moves this setup's heights (last row), and the depth comes from steel the op never sees as material.

## Expected

`Top of Model` / `Bottom of Model` are the **part(s)**: the models the op machines (or the setup's non-fixture models). They never include fixtures, accessories, plates, vises, or a stock-source model. A fixture placed in setup B never changes setup A's heights.

**Done means:** with a built-in vise (and an imported fixture) placed, a default 2D Contour on a part resolves Bottom of Model to the part bottom and Top of Model to the part top, in the setup that holds the fixture and in any other setup. A pinning test generates a contour with and without a vise and asserts identical Z levels. The same holds for every kind whose heights default to the model references.

Related: #339 (fixtures/vises), #1094 (a stock-source model judged as a part - the same "which models are the part" question).
